text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS

- The cabinet decided at its regular meeting Thursday to underwrite a 12 billion forint state guarantee to Postabank. The cabinet also passed the privatisation concept for Mezobank and rubber stamped a contract for missiles which Defence Minister Gyorgy Keleti signed with the French firm Matra Defence.

- Prime Minister and Socialist Party president Gyula Horn and the entire national board of the party absolved Civil Secret Services Minister Istvan Nikolits from any political responsibility for the way he handled the Operation Birch Tree case.
- Screening committees have established that several MPs are suspected of having worked as secret agents in the past.
- The NATO Council decided in Brussels on Thursday to invite all 27 countries involved in the Partnership for Peace project to the alliance's summit meeting in Madrid.
- Production at the Suzuki plant in Esztergom is to be stepped up by 8,000 cars to 60,000 cars this year, president Osamu Suzuki said at the general meeting of the Hungarian subsidiary yesterday.
- The number of enterprises operating in Hungary went down by five percent to 720,000 in the first quarter.
- The first quarter results of Pannonplast Rt. were a considerable improvement compared to January-March 1996.
- A gang of software pirates was arrested yesterday in Gyor.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- Interior Minister Gabor Kuncze will shortly meet heads of party parliamentary groups to learn which provisions of the electoral law they wish to see amended.

- President Arpad Goncz and Romanian President Emil Constantinescu will together unveil a memorial column in Snagov, Romania late next month in tribute to one-time Hungarian premier Imre Nagy and his associates who were held in detention there following the crushing of Hungary's 1956 uprising.
- Seven MIG-29s belonging to the Hungarian Armed Forces will fly to Poland shortly to take party in a shooting exercise.

- Hungary's GDP and real wages will probably show respective increases of three percent and one to two percent next year, according to the government's draft economic programme for the years 1998-2000. The economic cabinet will also discuss the possibility of introducing a more stringent anti-inflation package.
- After a "staggering" performance over the past six years, Hungary is economically speaking already an integral part of the EU, said Istvan Pataki, deputy state secretary at the Foreign Ministry.
- The foreign trade deficit decreased slightly, but that of the central budget substantially worsened in the first quarter compared to the same period of 1996, the Central Statistics Office reports.
- The AGM of the chemical giant BorsodChem Rt will accept the 1996 balance sheet spelling out 5.6 billion forints after-tax profits today.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- Shareholders of Inter-Europa Bank Rt. will get a 12.5 percent dividend on last year's profits.
- The government will porobably decide to transfer the 21,100 hectares of land owned by the agricultural group Babolna Rt. into public ownership before the firm's privatisation.
